claims.claim: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV applied as a scoped env prefix: the POSIX-style argument survives INTACT into the native child's argv (suppression works), and WITHOUT the prefix the same argument is MSYS-converted to a Windows path (normal conversion works). Both hold in one probe.

Both-states control (regression seed windows-shell.md:11): with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV exported globally, a path-carrying command demonstrably receives the UNCONVERTED POSIX path (a form no Windows path API accepts as absolute); without it, the argument arrives converted. The probe can see the inversion a global suppression silently causes.

Estate finding (measured 2026-10-26): C:\c is a junction to the drive root on this box, so every aliased /c/... path resolves regardless of suppression - a resolution-based probe would be UNABLE to see the global-suppression defect here; the probe therefore asserts on the child's received argument bytes, which is mechanically sound on any box.

negative_controls.description: Global export of MSYS_NO_PATHCONV flips the child's received argument from a converted Windows path to the raw POSIX path - the exact silent-inversion shape the scoped-suppression rule exists to prevent.

implementation.measured_lane: Git Bash (absolute binary pinned - the bare 'bash' name resolves to WSL bash when spawned from a Windows process and cannot see /c/... paths, rc=127) spawning a native python child that echoes its received argv bytes
implementation.child: probe-local echo_args.py prints received argv as JSON (one file per observation)
